clue.text: State school in a rut, after shake up, gets top grade

indicators.note: once these words have been given a shake up, their letters land in a new order

parts.note: A is the top grade in an exam or school report

explanation.surface: A school stuck in a rut is shaken up by new management and earns the best possible rating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in a rut' as a stuck school, but those words are simply part of the letters to be shaken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the Atlantic coast, whose capital is Columbia.

clue.text: Attach movie camera to part of body, and express oneself freely

definitions.text: Attach movie camera to part of body
definitions.meaning: read literally: film (shoot) with the camera held at your waist (the hip)
to speak bluntly and on impulse, without thinking first

explanation.surface: Strapping a film camera to your waist and speaking your mind sound like two odd tips for a vlogger.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from gunslingers firing without aiming, means to speak or act impulsively and candidly.

clue.text: Headdress not crown for the Pope,

indicators.note: the crown of a word is its top, so the headdress loses its first letter

parts.note: a turban is a wound cloth headdress

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the Pope swap his mitre for a plainer headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the 'crown' is the topmost letter, here the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban was the name taken by eight popes, Urban II having launched the First Crusade.

clue.text: Conned about politician's non-alcoholic drink in London district

indicators.note: the first word's letters go about, that is around, the next pieces

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled, so conned gives had
MP is a Member of Parliament, so the politician's gives MPS
tea is the classic British non-alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone was tricked over an MP's soft drink somewhere in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy, well-to-do area of north London famous for its Heath.

clue.text: Incidental music producer, foreign one, taking part in performance

indicators.note: the music producer and foreign one take part in, that is sit inside, the performance

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
a DJ (disc jockey) produces music at a club or on air
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Background music is produced by a visiting artist joining in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incidental music' looks like one phrase, but 'Incidental' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added but subordinate, supplementary rather than essential.

clue.text: Minor risks with potted plant

indicators.note: potted means abridged or cut down, so only a part of the words minor risks is kept

explanation.surface: A gardener warns that a houseplant in a pot carries small hazards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potted plant' reads as one phrase, but 'potted' signals the abridgement and 'plant' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of iris whose fragrant root is used in perfume.

clue.text: This could be the solution to a rhinal problem

definitions.text: This could be the solution to a rhinal problem

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so these letters are puzzled into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical device is suggested as a cure for trouble with the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhinal' means of the nose; 'problem' scrambles TO A RHINAL, and the whole clue describes the device used for nasal trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for breathing in medicinal vapour, an obvious remedy for a blocked nose.

clue.text: Binding chief, captured by a tribe as intended

indicators.note: the first pieces are captured by, held inside, the later ones

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or extended family group
cording is cord used for binding
top means chief, as in the top man

explanation.surface: A tribal leader is tied up by his own people, exactly as they had planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding chief' reads as a chief being tied up, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'a tribe' splits so that the C of the tribe begins the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Going the way it was planned is going the way it was meant to.

clue.text: Unruly crowd captures a kingdom of old

indicators.note: the crowd captures, holds inside itself, the next piece

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd

explanation.surface: Rioters seize an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Moab was an ancient kingdom east of the Dead Sea, often named in the Bible.

clue.text: US student getting a third in music?

definitions.meaning: in American colleges a student's main subject is their ..., and the student is said to ... in it
a ... third is a musical interval of four semitones

explanation.surface: An American undergraduate earns a lowly degree classification in music.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'third' suggests a British third-class degree, but here it is the musical interval.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a major is both the main subject and, informally, a student specialising in it.

clue.text: Bumpkin would appear extremely dense in test

parts.words: would appear extremely dense in test
parts.note: set the bumpkin word inside the four letters of test, after the first, and the result is a superlative meaning most dense

explanation.surface: A country yokel looks very stupid when sitting an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer placed in TEST spells THICKEST, extremely dense.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsophisticated country person, a yokel.

clue.text: Substitutes suffer wrongdoing

definitions.meaning: read as two words: to stand (bear) sin

explanation.surface: Replacement players have to put up with foul play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deputises for another is said to take their place in this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Income squandered, alas, by railway

indicators.note: money squandered is scattered, so the letters of alas are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone laments wages frittered away on train fares.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular fixed pay from employment.

clue.text: Balls, of course, put back after game

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed after the game

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and balls

indicators.note: put back means the word for course is turned backwards

parts.note: a set is a course, as in a series of lessons or a set of exercises

explanation.surface: Croquet balls, naturally, are returned after the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns SET into TES; 'Balls' looks like part of the croquet scene but means rounded fried patties.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquettes are small rounded fried cakes of mashed food, often ball-shaped.

clue.text: Dance and music test's second part follows question and answer exercise

indicators.note: the picked letter follows, comes after, the other pieces

parts.note: a drill is a training exercise

indicators.note: the second letter of the word test is taken

explanation.surface: A music exam's second section comes after a question-and-answer practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A square dance for four couples, popular in the 19th century, and the tune for it.

clue.text: They're flaming remarkable things

definitions.meaning: things that burn or scorch, such as very hot days
informally, anything outstanding, like a blistering shot or a sensational performance

explanation.surface: Someone calls a set of blazing objects astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a cracking shot or blistering hot day is described with this word.

clue.text: Fool, namely, with nothing to lose

indicators.note: the phrase for namely has to lose the round letter for nothing

parts.note: to wit means namely, that is to say
O looks like zero, so nothing gives O

explanation.surface: A foolish person is described as someone with nothing to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Girl seems mean — oddly deficient

indicators.note: the words are deficient in their odd letters, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A young woman comes across as unkind and somewhat peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Record Today and turn off?

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
our age means the present day, the times we live in

explanation.surface: A listener records a morning radio programme and then switches it off.
explanation.walkthrough: Today is also a BBC radio news programme, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter or dishearten someone is to put them off.

clue.text: Contemptible people in jets

explanation.surface: Despised people are found inside aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for small or obnoxious people, and also spurts of liquid from a nozzle.

clue.text: Extremely ratty, this? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly flags a possible rearrangement of the letters
the extremities of ratty, its first and last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A clue wonders whether a bad-tempered mood is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: R and Y, the first and last letters of 'ratty', join THIS, and 'Possibly' rearranges the lot; the whole clue then defines.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for irritable or bad-tempered, the same as ratty.

clue.text: Brute gives expression of derision, then ducks

parts.note: yah is a jeering exclamation
in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so ducks give two O's

explanation.surface: A thug jeers and then dodges out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' suggests dodging, but in cricket a duck is a score of nought, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are brutish humans, hence a coarse, boorish person.

clue.text: Tract written by international group is out of the ordinary

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a common is a tract of open public land

explanation.surface: A pamphlet published by the United Nations is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' suggests a pamphlet, but it is a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual, rare, not ordinary.

clue.text: Legal expert's general habit

definitions.meaning: an Islamic scholar who gives rulings on religious law
a habit is clothing; what an army general wears off duty is civilian dress

explanation.surface: A lawyer's usual practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general habit' reads as a usual practice, but it is a general's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an Islamic jurist and, from that, plain clothes worn by someone usually in uniform.

clue.text: Fellow curled lip, confiscating drug

indicators.note: the reversed lip confiscates, takes and holds, the drug
a curled lip is turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A man sneers while seizing narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, standing for any chap.

clue.text: Back, and what it could make you when speaking?

indicators.note: when spoken, the word sounds like the one for the answer

parts.note: cheering home the one you backed could leave you with a rough, croaky voice

explanation.surface: A question about what supporting something might do to your voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'Back' stands for what you back at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: Punters back runners at the races, so the animal stands for the thing backed.

clue.text: Cadence in one of The Four Seasons

definitions.meaning: a ... inflection in voice or music
the American word for autumn, as in Vivaldi's set of concertos

explanation.surface: A musical close in a movement of Vivaldi's famous work.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a drop in pitch, and Americans call autumn by this name too.

clue.text: Homework outstanding before term — one's engrossed in it

parts.note: prep is school slang for homework
o/s is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding
a session is a term, as of a court or school

explanation.surface: Schoolwork is still owed just before the term begins, and someone is buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A preoccupation, something that absorbs one's attention.
